# pAVF Auth Guide
## Insurance Authorization Reference

_Route: /pavf/auth-guide. Static reference page — no server calls, no cloud storage. Displays CPT codes, ICD-10 codes, and required documentation by payer type._

**Back to pAVF Compass**

## Insurance Authorization Guide
pAVF Compass™ — CPT 36836 / 36837 · SIR 2025 / KDOQI 2019

---

## Procedure Codes (CPT)

### CPT 36837 — RVU 9.07 — WavelinQ™ (BD)
Percutaneous arteriovenous fistula creation, upper extremity, separate access of both peripheral artery and peripheral vein

**Access:** Dual access — separate arterial and venous punctures

**Included in this code (do NOT bill separately):**
- All vascular access for the procedure
- Ultrasound and fluoroscopic guidance (imaging included)
- Radiologic supervision and interpretation
- Maturation procedures performed at the same session
- Balloon angioplasty of fistula creation site (if performed)

_Most commonly billed code for WavelinQ system. Category I CPT code effective January 2023._

### CPT 36836 — RVU 7.20 — Ellipsys® (Medtronic) — historical; device discontinued
Percutaneous arteriovenous fistula creation, upper extremity, single access of both peripheral artery and peripheral vein

**Access:** Single access — one puncture site for both artery and vein

**Included in this code (do NOT bill separately):**
- All vascular access for the procedure
- Ultrasound guidance (imaging included)
- Radiologic supervision and interpretation
- Maturation procedures performed at the same session

_Ellipsys device discontinued. Code may still be used if single-access technique is employed._

---

## ICD-10 Diagnosis Codes

| Code | Description | Usage Notes | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| N18.6 | End-stage renal disease (ESRD) | Primary diagnosis. Required for all pAVF claims. Patient must be on dialysis or imminently requiring dialysis. | Primary |
| Z99.2 | Dependence on renal dialysis | Use when patient is already receiving hemodialysis via catheter or other temporary access. | Secondary |
| N18.5 | Chronic kidney disease, stage 5 | Use when patient has CKD Stage 5 but has not yet initiated dialysis (pre-emptive access creation). | Secondary |
| T82.49XA | Other complication of vascular dialysis catheter, initial encounter | Use when prior catheter complication (infection, thrombosis, dysfunction) is driving the need for permanent access. | Secondary |
| Z87.39 | Personal history of other endocrine, nutritional and metabolic diseases | Secondary code for relevant comorbidities (diabetes, hypertension) contributing to CKD. | Secondary |
| I10 | Essential (primary) hypertension | Common secondary diagnosis. Include when hypertension is a contributing factor to ESRD. | Secondary |
| E11.65 | Type 2 diabetes mellitus with hyperglycemia | Include when diabetic nephropathy is the etiology of ESRD. | Secondary |

---

## Prior Authorization Requirements by Payer

_Tabs: Medicare FFS · Medicaid · Private / Commercial_

### Medicare (Fee-for-Service)
**Coverage Status:** Covered — No Prior Auth Required (FFS)  
**Prior Auth:** No Prior Auth (FFS)

**Overview:** Traditional Medicare (Parts A and B) covers percutaneous AV fistula creation under CPT 36836 and 36837 as Category I CPT codes, effective January 1, 2023. There is no National Coverage Determination (NCD) or Local Coverage Determination (LCD) specifically for pAVF. Coverage is based on the general principle of medical necessity for ESRD dialysis access. No prior authorization is required for Medicare Fee-for-Service.

**Prior Auth Note:** Medicare Fee-for-Service (Traditional Medicare) does NOT require prior authorization for CPT 36836/36837. These are Category I CPT codes effective January 2023. Claim is submitted post-procedure.

**Coverage Criteria:**
- Diagnosis of ESRD (ICD-10: N18.6) or CKD Stage 5 requiring imminent dialysis (N18.5)
- Patient requires permanent hemodialysis vascular access
- Procedure performed by a qualified physician with appropriate training (per SIR 2025 guidance: 2-hour didactic + 1-on-1 training + 3 simulated proctored cases)
- Procedure performed in a Medicare-participating facility (hospital outpatient, ASC, or office-based lab)
- Medical necessity documented in the medical record
- Vessel mapping performed confirming adequate anatomy (perforator vein ≥2 mm, superficial vein ≤6 mm depth, central veins patent)

**Required Documentation — Clinical Record (must be in chart):**
- Nephrology or treating physician note documenting ESRD diagnosis and dialysis need
- Vessel mapping report: perforator vein diameter (≥2 mm), superficial vein depth (≤6 mm), Barbeau test result, arterial calcification grade, central vein patency
- Barbeau test documentation (Type A, B, C, or D)
- Arterial Doppler waveform assessment
- Documentation of why pAVF is preferred (e.g., forearm veins unsuitable for surgical AVF, patient preference, surgical unavailability)
- Physician attestation of pAVF training completion (SIR 2025 GS-7)
- Informed consent

**Required Documentation — Billing Documentation:**
- Operative/procedure report documenting: device used, access sites, fluoroscopic and US guidance, fistula confirmation, any maturation procedures
- ICD-10 primary diagnosis code (N18.6 or N18.5)
- CPT code: 36837 (WavelinQ dual access) or 36836 (single access)
- Place of service code (hospital outpatient: 22; ASC: 24; office: 11)
- Modifier -26 if billing professional component only (facility setting)

**Submission Process:**
1. Perform procedure — no pre-authorization needed for Medicare FFS
2. Document procedure report including device, access sites, guidance modalities, and fistula confirmation
3. Submit claim to Medicare contractor (Noridian, CGS, Palmetto, etc.) post-procedure
4. Bill CPT 36837 (or 36836) with primary ICD-10 N18.6
5. If denied, submit appeal with operative report, vessel mapping, and medical necessity letter citing SIR 2025 guidance

**Common Denial Reasons:**
- Insufficient documentation of medical necessity in the medical record
- Missing vessel mapping report or inadequate documentation of anatomy
- Procedure billed with incorrect CPT code (e.g., using unlisted code 37799 instead of 36837)
- Medicare Advantage plan (not FFS) — these plans can have their own policies
- Facility not enrolled in Medicare or procedure performed outside covered setting

**Known Payer Policies:**
| Payer | Status | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Medicare FFS (Traditional) | Covered | No prior auth required. Category I CPT codes since Jan 2023. |
| Medicare Advantage (varies by plan) | Variable | Plans can create own policies. Some require prior auth. Verify with specific plan. |

**Billing & Authorization Tips:**
- Medicare FFS does NOT require prior auth — submit claim post-procedure with complete documentation
- Medicare Advantage plans are separate from FFS and may require prior auth or have non-coverage policies
- Always verify the patient's specific plan: Medicare FFS vs. Medicare Advantage (Part C)
- CPT 36837 includes imaging guidance — do NOT separately bill 76937 (US guidance) or 77001 (fluoroscopy)
- Subsequent pAVF maintenance procedures use CPT 36901–36909 (not 36837)
- RVU for 36837 = 9.07 (2025 Physician Fee Schedule)

**Reimbursement Note:** Medicare FFS reimbursement for CPT 36837: approximately $800–$1,200 (physician component) depending on geographic adjustment. Facility component billed separately by the hospital/ASC.

### Medicaid
**Coverage Status:** Generally Covered — Prior Auth Usually Required  
**Prior Auth:** Prior Auth Required

**Overview:** Medicaid coverage for pAVF (CPT 36836/36837) varies by state. Most state Medicaid programs cover the procedure as a medically necessary dialysis access intervention, but prior authorization is typically required. **Billing & Authorization Tips:**
- Always verify coverage BEFORE scheduling — many commercial plans deny pAVF
- Request peer-to-peer review immediately after denial — this is your best opportunity to reverse
- Use the pAVF Compass Appeal Letter generator to create a guideline-based appeal
- Cite CPT Category I status (Jan 2023) and Medicare coverage as evidence of mainstream acceptance

**Reimbursement Note:** Commercial reimbursement for CPT 36837 varies widely. Plans that cover pAVF typically reimburse at 110–150% of Medicare rates. Negotiate rates in your payer contracts specifically for 36837 given the procedure complexity.
